name: Multi-Round Waterfall and Implied Valuation

positioning.oneLineSummary: Values a later-round claim only after reconstructing every prior round, the complete payoff stack, and the exit-value distribution.
positioning.productLabel: Multi-Round Waterfall Lens — based on Metrick and Yasuda's public AUTO/FLEX architecture
notAClaimOf: the newest round having standalone economics
an option model eliminating term or data uncertainty

attribution.display: Based on Andrew Metrick and Ayako Yasuda's public later-round, partial-valuation, and implied-valuation architecture

neutralParaphrase: A later-round investment sits inside a stack of prior securities whose preferences, participation, conversion, caps, seniority, and share counts interact. The complete stack first produces a piecewise exit waterfall. Estimating current partial value additionally requires an exit-value distribution and option-model assumptions. The resulting security value and implied post-money should be shown separately from common-equity intrinsic value and headline round valuation.

requiredConditions: All prior and current rounds are represented from governing documents.
The exit waterfall reconciles before present-value modeling.
Total exit value, volatility, rate, holding-period distribution, and model choice are explicit assumptions.
Common-equity value, each security's partial value, and implied post-money are separately labeled.
Model risk and legal ambiguity are surfaced.

requiredEvidence.description: Every round's securities, shares, investment, preference, seniority, participation, cap, conversion, dividends, triggers, and amendments.
Versioned distribution or scenario set for total distributable exit equity value and timing.
Model type, total value, volatility, risk-free rate, expected holding/expiration distribution, and calibration evidence.
Current investment amount, price, shares, rights, and reported pre/post-money values.

decisionQuestions: Are all prior rounds and amendments included?
Does the exit waterfall reconcile at every contractual breakpoint?
Which option components represent each security's payoff?
How sensitive is current partial value to volatility, timing, and total value?
What implied valuation follows from security-specific value?
How and why does it differ from headline post-money and common-equity value?
positiveSignals: All rounds reconcile to legal documents and the cap table.
Piecewise payoffs reconcile across a dense exit grid.
Option components reproduce the contractual payoff schedule.
Assumption and model sensitivities are visible.
Security-specific, implied, headline, and common values are separately reported.
redFlags: Only the newest round is entered.
One deterministic exit point is presented as current partial value.
Volatility or holding period comes from an unexplained default.
Implied post-money is labeled company intrinsic value.
disconfirmingEvidence: A missing prior round materially changes breakpoints or proceeds.
The option decomposition fails to reproduce the waterfall.
Partial value is unstable under defensible volatility or timing inputs.
Legal interpretation changes seniority, participation, or conversion.
Security protections explain most of the headline valuation premium.
contraindications: Do not value a later round without all prior rounds.
Do not perform option valuation before verifying the contractual payoff.
Do not transfer preferred value to common shares.
Do not use an implied valuation as the deterministic investment decision.

instructions: Reconstruct and reconcile the complete security stack.
Decompose each payoff into supported option components if current partial value is required.
Run model and sensitivity calculations in deterministic services.
Report security, implied, headline, and common values separately and pass them to Fund Policy.

sourceReliability.low: Only reported rounds and headline values are known.
sourceReliability.medium: Most legal terms exist but one prior round or model input is uncertain.
sourceReliability.high: Complete legal stack, cap table, valuation distribution, and calibrated model inputs are verified.

evidenceStrength.low: One exit point and generic terms drive the output.
evidenceStrength.medium: Waterfall is verified but present-value assumptions remain broad.
evidenceStrength.high: Waterfall, component reproduction, and sensitivities pass deterministic tests.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only current-round investment and price are covered.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Rounds and payoffs are covered but timing or volatility is incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: All rounds, claims, breakpoints, distributions, model inputs, GP/LP terms, and reported values are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: The round stack or security cannot be reconstructed.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: The stack is usable with one flagged legal or model ambiguity.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The complete transaction and valuation context are explicit.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only a missing-document request can be produced.
judgmentConfidence.medium: A provisional payoff or partial-value range is available.
judgmentConfidence.high: Security-specific and implied values are reproducible and reconciled.

promotionRequirements: Validate option and waterfall models with valuation experts and venture counsel.
Reconcile historical test cases against legal documents and realized payoffs.
empiricalQualifications: Private-company exit distributions, volatility, and timing are difficult to observe.
Option valuation can be highly sensitive to model choice and inputs.
Reported post-money values may materially overstate common-equity value.

rights.notes: The public companion-tool architecture is neutrally paraphrased; formula and legal fidelity require third-edition and expert review.

openIssues: Specify validated option models, calibration data, and legal term taxonomy.
